top_news.title: Microsoft reacts to US immigration crackdown while Trump honours Nadella
top_news.summary: Microsoft on Thursday (local time) responded to the Trump administration's immigration crackdown after being suspended from the Permanent Labour Certification Program, while US President Donald Trump honoured Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Microsoft, in its response, said it believes in the "strength and talent of the American workforce" and highlighted that the vast majority of its US employees are Americans. The statement came as Trump praised Nadella for his leadership and role in transforming Microsoft. On recent immigration questions, Microsoft issued a statement saying, "We believe in the strength and talent of the American workforce. That is why the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans." "We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. These were not to hire new people," the company further said. Microsoft said the remaining H-1B filings for new employees involved people who were already legally present in the United States and chose to join the company. "They are not new arrivals to our country," it said, adding that these employees accounted for only one per cent of Microsoft's US workforce. The company said it only files H-1B petitions for employees who meet the "rigorous standards" of the visa category and disputed any suggestion that its foreign workers were being paid less than other employees. "We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work," Microsoft said. "Microsoft succeeds as a global technology leader by developing the world's best technology workforce. We do this by strengthening this country's talent pipeline, hiring American workers, and attracting the best talent from around the world," it added. articles.title: Microsoft reacts to US immigration crackdown while Trump honours Nadella
articles.summary: Microsoft on Thursday (local time) responded to the Trump administration's immigration crackdown after being suspended from the Permanent Labour Certification Program, while US President Donald Trump honoured Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation. Microsoft, in its response, said it believes in the "strength and talent of the American workforce" and highlighted that the vast majority of its US employees are Americans. The statement came as Trump praised Nadella for his leadership and role in transforming Microsoft. On recent immigration questions, Microsoft issued a statement saying, "We believe in the strength and talent of the American workforce. That is why the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans." "We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees. These were not to hire new people," the company further said. Microsoft said the remaining H-1B filings for new employees involved people who were already legally present in the United States and chose to join the company. "They are not new arrivals to our country," it said, adding that these employees accounted for only one per cent of Microsoft's US workforce. The company said it only files H-1B petitions for employees who meet the "rigorous standards" of the visa category and disputed any suggestion that its foreign workers were being paid less than other employees. "We pay our employees some of the highest compensation in the tech sector, and our wages are among the highest of all H-1B filings. We pay our H-1B employees the same as any other employees doing comparable work," Microsoft said. "Microsoft succeeds as a global technology leader by developing the world's best technology workforce. We do this by strengthening this country's talent pipeline, hiring American workers, and attracting the best talent from around the world," it added.
